title: The Surgeon and Her Daughters by Chris Gabo at Theater 154 #thesurgeo...
transcript: Last night, I saw The Surgeon and Her Daughters at Theatre 154. In this new play, we see a chance encounter that becomes a one night stand. But this is just the inciting event for what becomes a series of unexpected connections among an eclectic group of characters — very on brand for its New York setting. It's actually a pair of sisters who emerge as the centerpiece of the story, though their relationship is arguably more fractured than familial. I liked this play's exploration of loss and destabilization and its underlying commentary on the uphill battle of cultivating empathy under a capitalistic war machine, aka the United States. Thematically, it feels very relevant. However, I felt the plot was too disjointed to fully realize these concepts and that the scene work wasn't efficient enough to allow you to connect the dots while you're actually watching the piece. For a second preview, things ran pretty smoothly, but I do hope they can tighten it up so its themes can properly shine through. With that, another program for my collection.
